ety.text: From veretrum (“penis; genitals”) + -lus (diminutive suffix). As it is first attested in Apuleius, it may have been a neologism coined by him, possibly intended as a translation of Greek βάλανος (bálanos, “glans, penis”), to refer to a type of shellfish that visually resembled a human penis. Editors differ on whether the passage where this word occurs should be read with feminine singular accusative "veretillam" or neuter singular accusative "veretillum", or even neuter plural accusative "veretilla".
